title: Behavioural problem-solving in 3D space derives from older problem-solving in other spaces

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Behavioural problem-solving in 3D space derives from older problem-solving in other spaces

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Problem-solving behaviour of animals in three-dimensional space is proposed to be a variant of an evolutionarily more ancient capacity to solve problems in metabolic, physiological, transcriptional and morphogenetic spaces.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Specific Conceptual Components of the Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere Framework

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It is proposed that the traditional problem-solving behavior we see in standard animals in 3D space is just a variant of evolutionarily more ancient capacity to solve problems in metabolic, physiological, transcriptional, and morphogenetic spaces (as one possible sequential timeline along which evolution pivoted some of the same strategies to solve problems in new spaces).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Specific Conceptual Components of the Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere Framework”. Scope: Evolution of problem-solving capacities across life

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.33

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Restricted evolutionary and mechanistic components can be examined, but the central derivation claim spans deep time and heterogeneous domains. Existing data have weak power to distinguish inheritance from analogy or convergence.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define common algorithmic signatures of search, error correction, and setpoint pursuit across molecular, morphogenetic, and locomotor tasks, then test phylogenetic ordering and mechanistic homology against independent convergence models.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Shared signatures do not establish evolutionary derivation.

Problem-solving across spaces is strongly analogy-dependent.

Behavior and molecular regulation rarely have matched comparative data.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.38
analysis feasibility: 0.35
data existence: 0.42
discriminating power: 0.3
data adequacy: 0.18

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public orthology and divergence-time resources can test whether components of physiological and morphogenetic control are older than nervous systems. That is a proxy for the proposed timeline. The claim that 3D behavioral problem-solving is the same strategy pivoted into a new space is not distinguished by gene age alone.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Date gene families used in physiological and morphogenetic control against the origin of nervous systems and 3D behavioral circuits; the sequential claim is supported only as a proxy if those families are older and later co-opted into neural control.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Shared genes are compatible with later co-option and do not show that behavioral strategies are variants of older ones.

Problem-solving in metabolic or morphogenetic space is not a variable in these databases.
